_README: Provider blocks parked here so they can be re-enabled without losing the
exact known-good config. As of 2026-07-13 the active set in bifrost/
config.json is: vllm-local + embed-local + nvidia-nim + openrouter +
hf-router + cerebras + groq + mistral + zai + github-models (10 total,
github-models added 2026-07-13). (gemini + moonshot both
parked — see below.) ALL-FREE stack — no paid providers. Everything
else is shaped here for fast restoration.
moonshot   — PARKED 2026-06-11. Was the only PAID provider. Kimi K2.6
is now free via nvidia-nim/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (40 RPM,
200 on request) so paid Moonshot was removed. KIMI_API_KEY
blanked in shared-infra/.env; operator to cancel Moonshot
billing/auto-recharge. Restore this block + key + compose
passthrough to re-enable.
anthropic  — env empty; user disabled intentionally.
Status (2026-07-13, Perf-503b-W3b — VK/provider health sweep):
moonshot-nim-compat — PARKED 2026-07-13. This is a SEPARATE block from
the paid 'moonshot' above — it's the free NIM-compat shim
that lived in config.json as provider name 'moonshot' from
2026-06-11 to 2026-07-13. Parked because NVIDIA NIM 404s
moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 with 'Function ... Not found for
account' on BOTH API keys despite it being listed in
/v1/models — confirmed upstream NVIDIA bug, not a config
problem. nvidia-nim/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 was LEFT ACTIVE
in the nvidia-nim provider block itself (NIM's own catalog
still lists it); if NVIDIA redeploys the function it just
starts working again with zero config change. See the
moonshot-nim-compat block's own _comment for the exact
restore steps + a re-verify curl.
gemini     — was ACTIVE since 2026-05-31 (FLASH-ONLY as of 2026-06-11:
gemini-3.x Pro previews are billing-gated, no free API
tier since ~May 2026). PARKED 2026-07-08 — GEMINI_API_KEY
invalid/expired, was flooding logs at ~4 warn/min. The
'gemini' block below in this file IS the exact known-good
flash-only config that was live (verified 2026-07-13 — its
models[] matches config.json.bak.parkgemini-20260708 byte
for byte). Restore: refresh GEMINI_API_KEY at
https://aistudio.google.com/apikey, copy the block below
back into config.json's providers, run
sync_vk_allowlists.py, restart. The wildcard block below
re-enables Pro IF billing is ever added.
minimax    — key still active upstream as of 2026-05-14 but user wants
it disabled. Either blank MINIMAX_API_KEY in shared-infra/
.env or revoke at MiniMax dashboard before restoring.
(MiniMax M2.7 is available FREE via nvidia-nim instead.)
openrouter — ACTIVE again since 2026-05-27 with a curated :free list
in config.json (refreshed 2026-06-11; one-time $10 topup
applied → 1,000 free req/day). The wildcard block below
is only for routing PAID OpenRouter models.
FREE perpetual-tier providers added 2026-05-31 (ready-to-enable recipes):
groq      — GROQ_API_KEY      (https://console.groq.com/keys; ~30 RPM, json_schema+tools)
cerebras  — CEREBRAS_API_KEY  (https://cloud.cerebras.ai; ~1M tok/day, 8K ctx)
mistral   — MISTRAL_API_KEY   (https://console.mistral.ai; ~1B tok/month, codestral)
gemini    — GEMINI_API_KEY    (https://aistudio.google.com/apikey; best json_schema; native provider block below)
These are OpenAI-compatible custom providers; Bifrost appends /v1 so the
base_url omits it. Gemini uses the native gemini provider block (models:[*]).
TO RE-ENABLE one of these providers:
1. Set / refresh the corresponding env var in shared-infra/.env:
anthropic  → ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
gemini     → GEMINI_API_KEY
groq       → GROQ_API_KEY
cerebras   → CEREBRAS_API_KEY
mistral    → MISTRAL_API_KEY
minimax    → MINIMAX_API_KEY
openrouter → OPENROUTER_API_KEY
2. Add the matching env var passthrough back to
docker-compose.bifrost.yml under `environment:` (as of 2026-07-13
the compose file already passes NV_API_KEY/NV_API_KEY_2,
OPENROUTER_API_KEY, HF_TOKEN, CEREBRAS_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY,
MISTRAL_API_KEY, ZAI_API_KEY, GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN, and
GEMINI_API_KEY through for the parked gemini block -- add only
the provider-specific key if it is not already in that list).
3. Copy the block from this file into the `providers` object in
bifrost/config.json.
4. Restart Bifrost:
docker compose -f shared-infra/docker-compose.bifrost.yml restart bifrost
5. Smoke-test:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4445/v1/chat/completions \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{"model":"<provider>/<model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ok"}],"max_tokens":10}'
Why these are disabled-here-but-listed, not deleted:
Bifrost runs a model-discovery loop on startup AND every minute. With
invalid / missing keys, that floods logs at 4 warn/min × invalid_
provider_count. Cheaper to leave the blocks here as recipes.

moonshot-nim-compat._comment: PARKED 2026-07-13 (Perf-503b-W3b) — NOT the same block as 'moonshot' above (that's the retired PAID api.moonshot.ai account). This was the free NIM-compat-shim provider named 'moonshot' in config.json from 2026-06-11 to 2026-07-13, routing legacy `moonshot/kimi-*` callers to NVIDIA NIM's moonshotai/kimi-k2.6. Parked because NVIDIA NIM now 404s that model with 'Function 23d4f03a-b8a6-4adb-a183-7daa083a09cc: Not found for account' on BOTH NV_API_KEY and NV_API_KEY_2 despite it still being listed in GET /v1/models — confirmed via direct curl to integrate.api.nvidia.com, bypassing Bifrost entirely, so this is an upstream NVIDIA catalog/serving-function bug, not a Bifrost or key problem. nvidia-nim/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 itself was left ACTIVE in config.json's nvidia-nim provider block (NIM's own catalog still lists it — if NVIDIA redeploys the function it starts working again automatically with zero config change). TO RESTORE this compat-shim block: rename the key back to 'moonshot', copy it into config.json's `providers` object (in place of where it was, before `zai`), run sync_vk_allowlists.py, restart shared-bifrost. Re-verify first: curl -s -X POST https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer '$NV_API_KEY -d '{"model":"moonshotai/kimi-k2.6","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"max_tokens":4}' — expect HTTP 200, not 404.
